question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), what is the maximum total duration a person can be kept in police custody?
solution:
The correct answer is __**90 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)** is a proposed replacement for the colonial-era **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973**. It aims to modernize and simplify criminal procedures in India.
 
• Under the BNSS, the **maximum total duration for which a person can be kept in police custody is 90 days**.
 
• This timeframe of **90 days** is in line with the provisions under the existing **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) Section 167(2)**, which states that in cases where the investigation relates to an offense punishable with imprisonment for a term of ten years or more, the accused can be held in custody for a maximum of 90 days.
 
• For offenses with lesser punishments, the custody period is reduced to **60 days** as per the CrPC. However, this limit may vary in some cases
